rationale: B wins because it does the adult thing: it keeps the angles closer to the supplied facts and makes the missing proof do real work. Its best headline, "REI is putting trade-in and gear repair in all 180+ stores — and betting resale is now a co-op fixture, not a pilot," is a clean retail-operations story; A's "As outdoor gear floods secondhand apps" imports an outside market narrative the update never gave it. A has more breadth, but breadth is not a license to smuggle in the pitch you wish you had.
gaps_in_A: "As outdoor gear floods secondhand apps" is the biggest foul. The update gives no evidence that outdoor gear is flooding apps, that third-party resale is the live competitive peg, or that REI is trying to pull volume back inside.
"public retailers can't easily replicate" overstates the co-op thesis. The facts say REI is member-owned and not publicly traded; they do not prove public retailers cannot scale resale or repair.
"Both announcements ... are live this week" adds timing the packet does not supply. The update says the dividend was issued this year, not that both items broke this week.
"stores already navigating union campaigns" makes current activity sound confirmed. The update only says REI has faced unionization activity at several stores.
gaps_in_B: "operational and floor-space commitment competitors get benchmarked against" gets ahead of the evidence. Floor space, staffing, and competitor benchmarking are proof needs, not facts yet.
"several stores see union drives" and "workers organize" sharpen the labor angle by making the activity sound current. The packet only says REI has faced unionization activity at several stores.
B misses the member-economics angle A found: dividend plus trade-in credit plus repair access as the practical value of co-op membership. That is a real consumer-finance lane.
"resale is now a co-op fixture, not a pilot" is close, but still needs care. All-store rollout supports it; permanence does not, unless REI confirms ongoing staffing, space, and program commitment.
